hbm_single_chip.note: 26 findings at first lowering, then 0. The five causes were all general: a scratch sized at one query row instead of the query block; a token-block round-up applied to a context-resolved leading axis, in the plan and in the emitter both; a cache_row spelling the HBM checker compared raw while the ROM checker already resolved it through CACHE_ROW_ALIASES; and a pooled state member map that recorded the LAST window of a repeated resource where the layer term walks from the first. None of them is model-specific and both shipped plan digests are unchanged.

rom_array_64.reason: region 'rom.r0.p059.s1' has 12 members per slot, which do not divide into 64 owners. The reduction scales n_routed_experts by the width factor, 192/16 = 12. This is a property of the reduced vehicle, not of the array backend -- the released 192 divides 64 three ways -- and it is a reduction-rule choice: an expert count is an ownership unit as well as a size, so a vehicle intended for an N-owner array has to keep it divisible by N, which at 64 owners means a width factor of at most 3 rather than 16.

what_this_is: The first admitted deployments of any DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash graph, on two of the three stores. The vehicle is the reduced fixture (dim 160, vocab 4,040, 40 layers, window 128, 12 routed experts), so these are shape-reduced deployments of the full operator set at shipped arithmetic, not shipped dimensions. Neither is a token: a token additionally needs the RTL issue bridge to admit the operations the graph names, which is measured in deepseek_v41_reduced_rtl_token_gap.json.
